tables.title: Where you fight it
rows: Howling Woods, Singer's Meadow, Rainy Plains, Humbler Huskland, Lullaby Hills, Frozen Highlands, Honeycomb Fields

tables.title: Moves
rows: Lunges in for two bites about a second apart (the second one hits for 18) and re-aims at you between them, so one dodge won't clear both. It only bites at close range and can go again 3 seconds later.

Its answer to you keeping your distance: after a short wind-up it runs at you for up to 4 seconds and hits with heavy knockback. It can only turn 20 degrees a second mid-charge, so sidestep late instead of running.

Ends a charge with a horn ram into a narrow cone in front of it, and also uses the ram on its own at mid range. A shockwave slam follows straight after when that's off cooldown, so be ready for the rings.

Marks ten strike points in a ring around itself, then ten more in a wider ring. Each one flashes for 1.75 seconds before a short ripple of lightning spreads from it and applies Zapped, and the ripples can be jumped or rolled through.
Winds up for about a second and a half, then fires three bolts across a 45-degree spread in front of it. The bolts don't home, so step sideways out of the spread rather than backing away along it.

Each thunderbolt drops a strike marker along its path five times a second, and every marker blows up 2 seconds later and applies Zapped. The path stays dangerous after the bolt has passed, so don't cut back across it.
Calls 6 to 8 Copper Cubes into the arena after a 2-second wind-up, with never more than 16 alive at once. It often comes right after a thunderbolt volley.

Builds from the moment it spawns, with visible charge-up stages at 16 and 18 seconds. At 20 seconds it bursts, applying Zapped and a light shove to anyone close, then it moves at double speed with 50% faster melee for 10 seconds; the burst reaches about as far as its bite, so back off at the second stage.
